executiveSummary: Guidance remains stable at provisional Elevated 47/100. Central Illinois has a same-day heavy-rain and thunderstorm outlook, but the latest collection snapshot contains no active alert matched to the three confirmed Illinois facility counties and no disruption is established. A Milwaukee County river-flood watch remains an unscored location-verification lead because Watershed's exact Wisconsin municipality is not public.
baselineNote: Only genuine 17, 18, 19 and 20 September snapshots are available; four points are not a 30/90/365-day trend. Company exposure remains provisional and Cyber / OT remains unassessed.

observations.title: Central Illinois outlook adds locally heavy rain; facility-county guidance remains stable
observations.status: Reviewed; existing S07 guidance and factors unchanged
observations.finding: NWS includes McLean, Woodford and Tazewell in the 20 September central Illinois outlook. Periodic showers and thunderstorms may produce locally heavy rain and low-lying or poor-drainage flooding; stronger severe storms are mainly along and south of I-72. The 12:27 UTC collector snapshot contained no active alert matched to the three Illinois county SAME codes.
observations.causalPath: County-matched heavy rain and thunderstorms → possible local road or workforce access interruption → dispatch and production continuity. Actual route, utility and site effects remain unverified.
observations.sourceScope: County/zone outlook plus the latest collection snapshot only; absence of a matched active alert is not an operating clearance or proof of site conditions.
observations.decision: Refresh S07 evidence vintage and 24-hour expiry; retain all seven factors, action, trigger and guidance revision.

observations.title: Milwaukee County river-flood watch extends the regional Wisconsin verification lead
observations.status: Unscored regional verification lead; exact Watershed location unknown
observations.finding: NWS issued a Flood Watch for the Root River at Franklin in Milwaukee County, with flooding possible Sunday evening into Monday morning. This is a 19 September publication retrieved on 20 September, not a newly published 20 September event.
observations.causalPath: River rise in Milwaukee County → possible local road or workforce access interruption → conditional baking/popping continuity exposure if the unspecified Watershed operation is within an affected area.
observations.sourceScope: Watershed publicly identifies only a greater-Milwaukee presence. Exact municipality, building, routes, utility and any impact are unverified; the watch cannot be assigned to a facility.
observations.decision: Retain as a location-verification lead without changing Facility / weather factors. Escalate only if an operating location matches an applicable warning or verified disruption.

reviewNotes.revision: No outage, downtime, utility interruption, route closure or production loss is public. No capacity inference is added.

reviewNotes.revision: No new dated, applicable Watershed ingredient, supplier, customer, product or lot match was established. No food-safety score or hold guidance is changed.

reviewNotes.revision: CISA primary pages/feed remained inaccessible through the review path and no installed asset inventory is public. Cyber / OT stays null rather than zero.

reviewNotes.revision: Illinois outlook counties are explicit; alert matching uses Illinois SAME codes. The Wisconsin watch is restricted to a region-level lead. Existing triggers remain a matched warning, verified route closure, utility interruption or reported site impact.

manualChecks.result: Primary NWS outlook includes McLean, Woodford and Tazewell; heavy rain and thunderstorms are possible today, with the stronger severe risk mainly along and south of I-72.
Latest collector snapshot contained no active alert matched to Illinois SAME codes 017113, 017203 or 017179. Paducah-office heat-advisory text mentioning McLean referred to Kentucky and was rejected.
Root River at Franklin Flood Watch was retained as a Milwaukee County regional lead only; exact Watershed location and impact remain unknown.
The rolling page changed, but no newly dated company-applicable food recall or alert was established during review; page-change detection alone is not an event.
Current DATCP index still lists 18 September as the latest release; no later dated relevant state event was established.
EIA still reports the 15 September diesel release and schedules the next release for 22 September; S01 is unchanged.
Collector detected a page change, but the primary operations page did not expose a dated operating event in the readable review path; no grid condition is inferred.

reviewGaps: Eighteen collector states remain blocked/error (12 blocked, 6 fetch/parser errors); successful manual reads do not erase those failures.
CISA advisory and KEV pages/feed remained inaccessible through the review path; no current installed-asset applicability conclusion.
USDA WASDE/FAS, BTS/USACE/MARAD, FDA import, FSIS, DOL/SEC, local Gridley/Deer Creek, Flagstone, Rockwell and BLS automated gaps remain visible.
No public evidence identifies Watershed's exact Wisconsin municipality, named current supplier/customer, installed OT, production volumes or commissioned Deer Creek capacity.
